newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT-India gains on tight supply.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT-India gains on tight supply.

text.p: Indian global depositary receipts finished firmer on Thursday despite a sluggish showing in Bombay earlier, traders said.
They said GDRs picked up after a lacklustre start, and pushed ahead amid tight supply.
"It looked like it was drifting this morning and then at midday we moved ahead but there was not much volume. It seemed like a short squeeze," a trader said.
He said the market was running ahead of local stocks, building high premiums, and could come under pressure unless Bombay rallied.
Traders said gains came initially in SBI and TELCO, and others soon followed them higher.
Stocks in India were little changed, drifting slightly easier in dull trade. The Bombay 30 share index lost 4.23 points to 3,730.78.
The HSBC James Capel Indian GDR index closed 1.52 points up at 81.59, with the premium over the local market at 25.66 percent from 23.83 percent.
SBI posted a 47 cent rise to $25.00/26.00 and Hindalco collected 67 cents to $31.50/32.50.
The Capel Taiwan GDR Index rose 3.20 points, or 2.88 percent, to 114.43, representing a discount to the local market of 3.27 percent.
The Capel Korea GDR Index lost 0.10 points to 67.50 points, a premium of 39.28 percent over the local market.
